security_audit.summary: Static alerts were not active malware indicators. They are Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, placeholder secrets, example fetches, and relative imports in documentation. I found one semantic documentation risk: the profile upload example lacks full file validation before writing to a public path.

remediation.issue: The profile upload example lacks complete file validation.
remediation.suggestion: Add image MIME and extension allowlists, verify file signatures, generate server-side names, and serve uploads through controlled storage.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be copied without project review.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that install and codemod commands require user confirmation, dependency review, and local test validation.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete File Upload Validation in Example
semantic_findings.description: The profile update example checks file size but does not validate MIME type, file signature, or an extension allowlist before writing to public/uploads. Users copying the pattern could publicly serve unsafe files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited example performs a size check, derives the extension from avatar.name, and writes the buffer to a public uploads path. It is documentation rather than executable skill code, so this is a documentation risk rather than active exploitation.

content.user_title: Build React 19 Apps with Modern Patterns
content.value_statement: React 19 changes can make forms, Server Actions, and migration work confusing. This skill gives concise patterns, migration steps, and security guidance for modern React projects.
actual_capabilities: Explains React 19 Actions, Server Components, and new hooks.
Shows form patterns with useActionState and Server Actions.
Guides optimistic UI updates with useOptimistic examples.
Provides React 18 to React 19 migration steps and codemod guidance.
Covers security practices for secrets, validation, and client boundaries.
limitations: It may not reflect React releases after the bundled references.
Examples need project-specific validation before production use.
It does not run installs, codemods, or tests by itself.
It does not replace official React or framework documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan a React 19 Migration
use_cases.description: Create a staged upgrade plan with codemods, TypeScript fixes, and regression checks.

use_cases.title: Design Modern Form Workflows
use_cases.description: Use Actions and useActionState for pending states, validation, and server-side mutations.

use_cases.title: Review React 19 Architecture
use_cases.description: Check Server Components, Client Components, Suspense boundaries, and data flow decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain React 19 Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which React 19 features matter for a simple form-heavy app. Recommend where to use Actions, useActionState, and Server Components.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Form Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a React 19 signup flow for my Next.js app. Include pending states, validation, optimistic feedback, and server-side data handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from React 18 to React 19 for this project. Prioritize codemods, TypeScript fixes, tests, and rollout risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my React 19 Server Actions design for security. Check authentication, input validation, secret handling, data exposure, and unsafe client boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need to migrate a React 18 dashboard to React 19.
output: A staged migration plan that starts with React 18.3 warnings.
A checklist for codemods, TypeScript updates, framework changes, and test coverage.
A risk review for forms, refs, Server Components, and production rollout.

output_examples.input: I need a React 19 form with server validation.
output_examples.output: A recommended Actions design with pending state, validation flow, error handling, and server-side data mutation guidance.

output_examples.input: I want to add optimistic comments to a post page.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline for optimistic updates, server confirmation, rollback handling, and ownership checks.

best_practices: Keep secrets inside server-only functions and never pass them to Client Components.
Validate Server Action inputs and authorize every mutation.
Run codemods first, then verify breaking changes with project tests.
anti_patterns: Do not copy examples without adapting security and data validation.
Do not place secret values or server-only modules in Client Components.
Do not migrate straight to production without React 18.3 warnings and regression tests.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps build React 19 apps using Actions, Server Components, new hooks, migration steps, and security practices.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from React 18?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes upgrade steps, codemod guidance, TypeScript changes, framework notes, and testing reminders.

faq.question: Does it support Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for Server Components, Server Actions, Suspense, and Next.js 15 migration considerations.

faq.question: Will it run package installs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains install and migration commands, but execution requires a separate user or agent action.

faq.question: Is the guidance production ready?
faq.answer: It is a strong starting point. You still need project-specific validation, testing, and security review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
